methodological_rigor.justification: Design is a prespecified exploratory multiomic analysis nested in a single-arm, non-randomized phase 1 trial (CITN-12, n=30; only n=14 tracked to EOT; group 1 vs group 2 of n=9 vs n=5). The authors explicitly state no sample-size calculation ('no further statistical tests were done to predetermine the sample size') and that they were not blinded to outcomes, and no replicates were run at any timepoint. The group 1/group 2 stratification is defined post-hoc from transcriptomic clustering at EOT and then used to interpret baseline differences in HIV DNA, which inflates the apparent predictive signal. Statistically, methods are reasonable (GLM/edgeR with BH correction, GSEA with 1,000 permutations, LASSO with leave-one-out CV, Mann–Whitney/Wilcoxon/Spearman, ridge model with ρ=0.59 P=0.035, ComBat for RNA-seq batch effects), but effect sizes are not consistently reported, cohort heterogeneity (11 cancer types, variable EOT 44–315 days) is not formally adjusted for, and the n=5 in vitro healthy-donor assays use paired t-tests on five donors, which is underpowered for the mechanistic claims. These are serious limitations that place the study at the lower end of competent methodology.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a prospective, longitudinal observational analysis embedded within a single-arm phase 1 trial (NCT02595866) with pre-specified exploratory immunologic/virologic endpoints, which maps most closely to an individual cohort study (Oxford 2b); the preclinical in vitro healthy-donor arm is subordinate validation. Clinical relevance is high: PLWH with cancer are an underserved population, and the identification of a pre-therapy IFN/ISG signature that associates with reservoir decline after pembrolizumab has direct implications for patient selection in HIV-cure trials and for rational design of combination strategies (IL-15 superagonists, TLR agonists, TGFβ blockade). Endpoints include cell-associated HIV DNA, inducible HIV RNA, plasma viremia and tumor response (1 CR, 4 PR), which are patient-relevant surrogates in both oncology and HIV cure fields. The findings are not practice-changing but inform near-term translational development.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the best fit because the central claim is a biomarker (ISG/TLR module signature) that stratifies HIV reservoir outcomes after anti-PD-1; CONSORT is not applicable (non-randomized phase 1 already reported in Uldrick 2019/2022). The paper reports eligibility, cohort stratification by CD4 count, assay panels, timepoints, candidate biomarkers, outcome definitions and multivariable modeling with cross-validation, but lacks a formal patient-flow/CONSORT-style diagram, pre-registration of the specific biomarker hypotheses, prospective definition of group 1/group 2 cutoffs, and quantitative discrimination metrics (AUC, sensitivity/specificity). Data availability is explicitly addressed: a Zenodo deposit (ref 81, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.11200738) and planned GEO deposit for RNA-seq matrices are stated, software versions reported (R 4.4.0, Seurat, SingleR, MAST, edgeR, mixOmics, SCimilarity v1.1), and antibody catalog numbers listed in Supplementary Data 1 D11.

novelty_literature.justification: The empirical novelty is the integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, plasma cytokines, flow cytometry and in vitro validation to show that a pre-existing myeloid ISG/TLR signature plus induced effector CD8 responses associate with reservoir decline in PLWH-with-cancer after pembrolizumab. However, the parent CITN-12 cohort and its reservoir-reversal observations were already reported (Uldrick 2019, 2022; refs 27, 30), ISG signatures predicting PD-1 response are established (Boukhaled 2022, ref 47; Acha-Sagredo 2025, ref 38), TGFβ–IFN antagonism and type I IFN restriction of HIV are well documented (Sandler 2014, Grunwell 2018, Guerin 2019, Yim 2023), and ex vivo PD-1 blockade and HIV latency reversal was shown by Fromentin 2019 (ref 13). The study is a meaningful mechanistic extension and population-specific contribution (PLWH-and-cancer) rather than a conceptual or methodological first; the SCimilarity cross-dataset mapping is a nice methodological touch but not transformative.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear arc from systemic 24-hour effects to subset-specific scRNA-seq to in vitro validation; the abstract is quantitatively grounded (n=30, 29M/1F, 1 CR + 4 PR, 9/14 ISGhi at EOT) and accurately reflects the paper. Figure captions are detailed, standalone-interpretable, and specify statistical tests and sample sizes. There are minor issues: an abstract typo ('present in subsets of across subsets of'), occasionally long run-on sentences in the methods, and some overlapping prose between Methods 'Study design' and the Results opening paragraph. Overall it is publication-ready scientific writing.

key_strengths: Prospective, longitudinal multiomic profiling (bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, plasma cytokines, flow cytometry) in a well-characterized phase 1 CITN-12 cohort with embedded in vitro mechanistic validation
Clinically important, underserved population (PLWH with advanced cancer) with pre-registered trial (NCT02595866) and translational endpoints relevant to both oncology and HIV cure
Convergent evidence that pre-therapy and 24-hour ISG/TLR myeloid programs stratify HIV DNA decay, supported by SCimilarity mapping to ~1,000 external datasets and NicheNet ligand prioritization
Appropriate analytic choices (edgeR with BH correction, GSEA with permutations, LASSO/ridge with leave-one-out CV, mixOmics, ComBat batch correction) with code/data at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.11200738
key_concerns: Single-arm, non-randomized design with n=30 overall and only n=14 at EOT (n=9 vs n=5 for group comparisons); no power calculation, no blinding, and no replicates, so key subgroup inferences are underpowered
Group 1 vs Group 2 is defined post-hoc from EOT transcriptomic clustering and then evaluated at baseline, which risks circularity in the 'preexisting ISG signature predicts reservoir decline' claim
Marked clinical heterogeneity (11 cancer types, variable EOT 44–315 days, sex imbalance 29M/1F) is acknowledged but not formally adjusted for in the predictive models
Reporting lacks a CONSORT/patient-flow diagram, prospective biomarker-cutoff definition, and discrimination metrics (AUC, sensitivity/specificity) for the signature
In vitro validation relies on n=5 healthy donors with paired t-tests, which is a thin mechanistic foundation for the HIV-restriction claims
Novelty is incremental over prior CITN-12 reports (Uldrick 2019/2022) and existing ISG-response-to-PD-1 literature (Boukhaled 2022; Acha-Sagredo 2025)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically competent and clinically meaningful translational multiomics with convergent mechanistic validation, but constrained by small post-hoc subgroups, no control arm, and incremental novelty — tier 2 (e.g., Nat Commun / CCR / JCI class) with minor revisions is the highest plausible acceptance; tier 1 is precluded by the lack of randomization, modest sample size and post-hoc stratification.
